evidence: Skill check 1 defines the defect as 'numbered acceptance lists, a "shall/must" spec table, a feature matrix, or a build recipe (framework, file layout, endpoint list) instead of a product ask'. task/instruction.md is 5 lines / 116 words of first-person prose in three paragraphs with a use-case motivation: line 1 'I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files. The editor itself matters: I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source.'; line 3 'Please read the six notes in /instructions before building.' (six note files do exist); line 5 'Put the app in /app and serve the workspace at /. I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in.' It contains no numbered or bulleted list, no table, no feature matrix, no framework, file layout or endpoint list. The six /instructions notes are also continuous first-person prose under plain headings with no bullets, numbering or tables (e.g. overview.md:3 'stays current in each of them while I work', behaviour.md:11 'That refresh must not touch what I'm doing', integration.md:1 '# How I start the app'), and policy.md:3 explicitly declines a build recipe: 'You may choose the layout, labels, routes, database schema and error wording.' The only fixed technical facts are the runtime contract that workbook check 4 requires to be stated (integration.md:3 'node /app/server.js', port 3000, 'GET /api/health'; integration.md:9 'Use SQLite for persistent records', DB_PATH), which is not a framework/file-layout/endpoint-list recipe. Probes: a spec-sheet reading would need a list or matrix structure, and none exists in any of the seven public files; a conforming builder is free in frontend stack, routes and schema, so the ask does not dictate an implementation. Lesser points recorded as notes, not defects: (a) ui.md is dense (17 lines, 888 words) and enumerates many exact editor behaviours in a requirements register ('The caret must stay in view', 'Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent every line a selection touches as one undoable action'), and behaviour.md:3-13 likewise; it stays prose in a consistent owner voice and is detail a demanding editor user could plausibly write, but it is the closest the task comes to a specification. (b) instruction.md:3 '/assets/seed_data.json describes the starting scope; there is no starter app to finish' is slightly authorial phrasing rather than something a requester would naturally say. This row is a static reading check; no runtime measurement is required for it and none was used.
